Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses task-based fMRI in a social context (adult expert advice) and includes a healthy adult group (ages 18–45), the paper does not clearly report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map specifically identified as coming from the healthy adult group. The reported whole-brain voxelwise analyses focus on developmental (between-group) contrasts and age-related effects, and subsequent within-age-group tests are reported as ROI/extracted-beta comparisons. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I5 (a clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16, ages 25–49) that used movie stimuli depicting social/emotional interactions to probe perception/understanding of others and empathy, satisfying social-related task criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise intersubject correlation (ISC) maps and ISC-by-valence/arousal GLM maps with voxelwise FDR-corrected statistics (figures and supplemental tables), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=27, ages within 18–65) that used task-based fMRI to examine social interaction processing (cooperative vs. affective interactions). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports coordinate tables and figures (FWE-corrected and uncorrected results), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based functional MRI in healthy adults (N=19, ages 21–34) using naturalistic audiovisual movie clips to probe multiple social features (faces, bodies, biological motion, action, emotion, social interaction, pain, speech). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results and contrasts (e.g., social vs non-social; feature-specific maps) are reported and thresholded (p<0.05 FDR) with figures and ROI coordinates. The methods and results include whole-brain analyses (non-orthogonalized and orthogonalized regressors) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only findings. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (kinship-based affiliative vs nonaffiliative scenarios) with healthy adult participants (final N=27; ages within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FWE-corrected results, whole-brain and ROI-corrected contrasts) with tables/figures and coordinates. The full text includes methods, behavioral and imaging results, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range, and the article is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (maternal response to infant cry; attachment/affiliation), conducted in adults (primiparous mothers, mean age 24.1, within 18–65) who are described as not meeting current major depressive episode criteria at scanning. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (own cry > control/other cry) using FSL with cluster correction and presents coordinates, tables, and figures of activation clusters. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level results), and I6 (results clearly described with tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (social reasoning/theory-of-mind and emotion understanding) in healthy adult participants (N=45; ages 19-23). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects results, multiple-comparison correction, peak coordinates in Appendix A, and whole-brain maps/figures), satisfying requirements for whole-brain task-evoked maps from the healthy group. Results for social tasks are clearly described and contrasted with mechanical tasks. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only groups, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of perception of emotional facial expressions (social communication / perception of others), meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample includes 23 healthy adult human volunteers aged 24–34 (meets sample criterion). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (random-effects group analysis, voxel- and cluster-level thresholds, figures of group significance maps) and provides stereotactic coordinates (supplementary table), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures, and tables) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age-out-of-range-only, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=21, mean age 24) that uses action observation/execution paradigms probing mirror-system responses—relevant to social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task analyses (explicit whole-brain thresholding at p<0.001 uncorrected and ROI analyses with FWE correction) and provides peak coordinates/tables. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the reported neuroimaging results are presented primarily via ROI / small-volume-corrected analyses; the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy group (only ROI SVC results and an exploratory note about V1). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criterion I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map) is not met; I6 (acceptable whole-brain coordinate reporting) is not satisfied for primary task contrasts. Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on E2.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n≈36, ages ~21) using a social cognition task (viewing others in pain — perception/understanding of others/empathy). The manuscript includes whole-brain, group-level task activation analyses (pre-priming whole-brain FDR-corrected maps; post-priming whole-brain results reported) and provides coordinates/tables and ROI analyses. All inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results are described and reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (interpersonal resource conflict) using an event-related whole-brain fMRI design. Sample: healthy adult participants (final N=17, mean age 23.5), satisfying the age and healthy-sample requirement. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Human Conflict > No Conflict, Computer Conflict > No Conflict), thresholded statistical maps, conjunctions, and tables/figures with coordinates and cluster information. Results are not ROI-only, nor limited to connectivity or between-group contrasts. Full text contains introduction, methods (participants, stimuli, MRI acquisition/analysis), results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of abstraction/concretization using Why-How and Categories-Exemplars tasks that probe social-cognitive processing (e.g., action identification, mentalizing). Sample: 24 healthy adult participants (ages 18–27) reported separately. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts and conjunction analyses are reported (thresholds, cluster correction, tables of regions and figures). The full paper includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–65). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

The study uses task-based fMRI during attractiveness comparisons (a social judgment of others), includes a healthy adult sample (25 right-handed British women, mean age 23.46), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain contrasts, conjunctions, and tables/figures with coordinates). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results clearly reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages are within range, empirical data are presented). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This paper reports an fMRI study using a real-world social task (speed-dating) that probes social/affiliative processing and learning from romantic interest/rejection, meeting social-related task requirement. Sample includes healthy adult participants (scanned N=38, ages 19–31) with participant screening described, satisfying the sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., yes vs no; Match vs Unrequited), thresholding and cluster-correction, and tables of coordinates and figures, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social communication and intention understanding in healthy adults (N=23, mean age 24), using a task with communicative vs private actions. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., CInt > PInt; interaction effects) with stereotaxic coordinates, thresholding, conjunction and PPI results, and tables/figures describing activations. Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present, so full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (coordinates and figures provided). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, out-of-range sample) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-affective task (threat-of-shock while holding a friend, stranger, or alone) that directly probes social regulation of neural threat responding, satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=22, mean age 23.6), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses used to identify functional ROIs (cluster-wise tests with FSL, Z-threshold and cluster p-threshold) and provides ROI coordinates and statistical results (Table 1 and text), meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROIs only, are not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and the article is empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study that explicitly investigates social communication (perception and evaluation of different laughter types) using task-based fMRI with healthy adult participants (N=18, mean age 26). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses (contrasts CSL>TIC, TIC>CSL, CAT>COU, etc.), with statistical thresholds, cluster corrections, and coordinate results/tables/figures. Whole-brain activation maps and contrasts for the healthy participant group are clearly described and reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective. It uses task-based fMRI during social-related processing (compassion/reappraisal to images of others’ suffering) (I3). The sample comprises healthy adults aged 18–45 with results reported separately for the healthy groups (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (e.g., Group × Redistribution Rank whole-brain interaction, IPC and DLPFC clusters, whole-brain corrected results), satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain task-evoked map (I5). Results are described in the main text and figures/tables (I6). The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=31, ages 18–26) that uses a social task (gambling for self, best friend, antagonist) directly addressing social-related processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and ANOVA results with coordinates (MNI) and tables, and describes whole-brain contrasts and interaction effects (Person × Outcome) with small-volume correction for a priori regions. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (recognition of others’ ‘vitality forms’) in healthy adult participants (19 adults, ages 21–29). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., how vs what) with statistical thresholds (PFWE < 0.05) and coordinate tables/figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for task relevance (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and whole-brain group-level results reported (I5); whole-brain results are also presented in tables/figures (I6). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind/emotion/pain judgments) in healthy adults. Methods report task-based fMRI with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (univariate contrasts and MVPA), with statistical thresholds and reported maps/tables/figures (e.g., contrasts B>Ph, E>Ph, Pa>Ph; Tables and Figures provided). Sample: 46 healthy adult females (age 18–31). The paper provides full introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in figures/tables and text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses fMRI during a social-evaluation task (perception/understanding of self/peer evaluation); (I4) the sample includes healthy adult participants (ages extend to 22.9 years, i.e., adults within 18–65); (I5) the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (whole-brain mixed-effects analyses and corrected cluster results, e.g., MPFC activation and PPI results reported for the full healthy sample); (I6) whole-brain results are described in the text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only, not only connectivity, and the study reports within-group whole-brain task effects in a healthy sample. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception: participants (N=21 healthy adult males, ages 23–33) viewed and rated dyadic nonverbal interactions during task-based fMRI. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8 random-effects flexible factorial ANOVA) with contrasts and cluster-level corrected results and coordinate tables/figures for the healthy group. Core article content (introduction, detailed methods, behavioral and fMRI results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of social impression formation in healthy adults using task-based BOLD fMRI. Participants: N=19 healthy adults (mean age 19.1), within the 18–65 inclusion range. The study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (functional localizer contrast form impression > remember order; main 2×2 ANOVA in dmPFC ROI with whole-brain cluster-correction procedures and tables of coordinates are provided), with tables/figures and corrected cluster thresholds described. The task is social (impression formation/perception and understanding of others), satisfying the review’s constructs. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state-only, no patient-only sample, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6) and can be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-perception task (passive viewing of biological vs scrambled point-light displays), includes a healthy adult group (n=48, ages 20–35), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., biological>scrambled; Sex×Condition ANOVA) with tables/figures and cluster-correction details. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (implicit/explicit detection of eye-gaze and self-propelling motion; implicit mental-state inference task), conducted in healthy adult participants (ages 19–28). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and statistical maps/contrasts (e.g., E–O, S–X; PCA-based regressions) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction; results are presented in tables and figures. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: social-related fMRI tasks; I4: healthy adult sample 18–65; I5: whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps reported; I6: results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age-only, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (third-party punishment/attribution of intentions) relevant to perception and understanding of others (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=26; mean age 26±5.7) within the 18–65 range (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical analyses (GLM, random effects multisubject ANOVA) with thresholding (q[FDR]<0.05) and reports Talairach coordinates and figures for activations (R TPJ, R AI), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (passive viewing of faces vs objects) and includes a healthy adult sample (21 adults age 18–37). The paper reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (faces>objects) with voxelwise results and tables of coordinates (Table 3) describing whole-brain effects and regression of activation against age; FFA group metrics are reported separately for adults in Table 2. Whole-brain results are reported for the healthy sample and provided in figures/tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, task-evoked maps from the healthy group. Therefore I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (attribute framing/self and reflected perspectives) in healthy adults (ages 19–41). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., positive vs negative frames, frame-consistent vs inconsistent) with coordinate tables/figures and thresholding procedures. Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This full-text reports empirical fMRI studies of social-affective processing in healthy adult participants. The paper includes two group-level fMRI experiments (fMRI1, fMRI2) using a social/empathy visuo-tactile paradigm, with whole-brain random-effects analyses (fMRI1 reported whole-brain results; fMRI2 used independent localizer-based SVC but also performed whole-brain analyses and reports group-level task contrasts and coordinates). Samples consist of healthy adult participants (female undergraduates) reported separately for each experiment. Group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts for the healthy groups are reported (interaction contrasts, peak coordinates, and tables/figures). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Meets inclusion criteria: (I3) Uses task-based fMRI probing social processing (Dynamic Social Gesture task contrasting social vs nonsocial gestures, actor-orientation, face-visibility); (I4) Reports a sample of healthy adult participants (N=20, mean age 21.41, range includes adults within 18–65); (I5) Presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (TFCE with permutation testing, reported in figures/tables and text); (I6) Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, figures, and supplementary tables. No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are reported. Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy adult participants (ages 23–39) using a social-judgment task (ambiguous social interactions) — matching the review’s social-related task domain. This paper reports a voxel-based morphometry (structural MRI) study of grey matter volume and its correlation with proneness to moral sentiments in healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample comprises healthy adult participants aged 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (the study does not use functional MRI during a social-related task within this paper — the task was behavioral and structural MRI was acquired), I5 (the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked fMRI statistical maps from the healthy/control group; only a secondary analysis uses previously reported SSC-BOLD values from an earlier fMRI study in a subgroup, but this paper does not present unmasked whole-brain fMRI activation maps). Therefore it does not provide the required whole-brain task-based fMRI results for inclusion. No exclusion criteria from the list directly apply beyond failing required inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of explicit social trait judgments (trustworthiness, attractiveness) on vocal stimuli in healthy adults (N=44, ages 21–60). Stimuli and tasks clearly probe social-related processing. There is no indication of ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses nor restriction to special/clinical groups. Full text (methods, results) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/empathy in healthy adults (n=27, mean age 34), using task-based fMRI with naturalistic video stimuli assessing social/empathic processing. The paper reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain GLM contrasts, peak MNI coordinates, conjunction analyses, and figures of whole-brain activations—satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain task-evoked map (reported in text, figures, and coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adult whole-brain task activations). This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=15, ages 20–28) that includes social-related processing (social distance: friends vs acquaintances) and uses task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise searchlight analyses (cross-domain MVPA classification and representational similarity analysis) with statistical maps and cluster results (FDR-corrected) identifying right IPL and other regions; figures and tables present these whole-brain results. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion E2 met: the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) fMRI analyses with no unmasked, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study uses task-based fMRI of social processing — social closeness judgments with friends vs unfamiliar faces) and I4 (sample includes healthy adult participants aged 19–30). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level task activation maps are reported; fMRI results are presented via ROI extractions rather than whole-brain voxelwise contrasts). Although the full text is complete and the study reports task fMRI in healthy adults, failure to provide whole-brain, group-level task activation maps means it cannot be included in this meta-analysis.

This full-text fMRI study directly investigates social-related processing (self and peer evaluations; social domain), meeting I3. It includes a healthy adult sample (19 adults ages 22–31) reported separately, meeting I4. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked group analyses (2×4×3 whole-brain repeated-measures ANOVA, corrected via Monte Carlo/AlphaSim) with tables/figures of significant clusters and parameter estimates for the healthy groups, meeting I5 and I6. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables) is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met. Overall, the study provides whole-brain activation maps from healthy adults during a social task and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (causal attribution/mentalizing) in healthy adults. The sample consists of 20 healthy adults aged 18–41 (meets age/sample criterion). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment using a social-attribution task (subjects judged another’s awareness) in a healthy adult sample (n=50; ages 18–49), with subsequent group-level, whole-brain contrasts (H trials − E trials) reported and thresholded, plus tables of peak coordinates and figures. Whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps for the healthy/control group are clearly described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (MRI acquisition and analysis), Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (social exclusion, punishment/forgiveness) using Cyberball and a modified Dictator Game (I3). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participant ages are within 18–65, and this is an empirical study with original fMRI data. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self- and other-referential recollection), using task-based fMRI and addressing social cognition constructs. Participants were healthy adults (n=18, ages 19–29), meeting the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects), with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables/figures (Tables 2 and 3; whole-brain and ROI/SVC reported), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting requirements. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core content appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (intergroup competition, self vs. other moral processing) in healthy adults (N=21, Mage=23.1), satisfying I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with corrected thresholds and provides tables/coordinates of supra-threshold clusters (Tables 1 and 2), meeting I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: the study is not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, includes within-group whole-brain task activations, and is empirical with healthy adult participants. This fMRI study tested facial color processing (a form of social communication/perception of others) using task-evoked BOLD responses to natural vs. bluish faces in healthy adults (N=25, mean age 25.2). The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (natural-colored face vs. natural-colored scrambled image) and presents group-level activations (figures and table) used to define ROIs. Thus it meets: I3 (social-related task: facial color/social perception), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task contrast reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that uses a social feedback/task paradigm involving self- and other-related trait evaluations (social cognition). It reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE-corrected clusters, tables of activations and MNI coordinates) and describes preprocessing and GLM analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social processing (emotion alignment with an interaction partner) using an interactive social task. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=20; mean age ~24), and results are reported for the healthy scanner group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with clusterwise FWE correction across the entire brain and presents activation results in tables/figures (e.g., Tables 2–3, Figures 3–4). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception/understanding of others) using point-light dyadic displays and an orthogonal task, meeting the review's construct. Sample: healthy adult participants (ten right-handed males, ages 22–32) are reported separately — satisfies the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts ((atypical upright + atypical inverted) − (typical upright + typical inverted)) with cluster-size correction and tables/figures of activated loci, meeting whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and thus appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI study of a social task (ultimatum game) with healthy adult participants and reports group-level task activations (I3, I4, I6). However, all task fMRI statistical tests were performed within an a priori anatomical mask composed of 16 bilateral ROIs (wfu_pickatlas) rather than as an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise analysis. The paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only/masked analyses) and fails inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an fMRI experiment using social/empathy-induction traffic-awareness videos (social-related task). Sample: 20 healthy adult males (ages 20–28), meeting the 18–65 healthy adult requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (CV>NV) with FWE correction (p<0.05) and peak coordinates/tables/figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of cross-modal person recognition (voice-face) in healthy adults (N=16), so inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample) are met. However, the paper reports results focused on ROI-corrected voxelwise analyses and PPI connectivity; the authors state there were no significant results at P<0.05 FWE for the whole brain without the covariate, and all reported activations are reported with ROI-based FWE correction or limited to predefined ROIs. The review requires at least one group-level whole-brain (unmasked/whole-brain) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group (I5), which is not provided. Therefore this study meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. Exclusion criterion met: E2. Full text appears complete.

This study reports an fMRI task examining social sharing/affiliation (participants view emotional pictures either together with a friend or alone), meets the social-related construct (affiliation), and tests healthy adult participants (ages 20–33). The paper presents group-level task-evoked whole-brain analyses and reports whole-brain activations (e.g., DLPFC, precuneus) with appropriate correction as well as ROI results; these healthy-group whole-brain effects are clearly described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (repeated public good game probing social tie formation/other-regarding preferences). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FSL GLM, cluster-wise FWE correction) with MNI coordinates and tables/figures. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (feeling addressed) that meets all inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper).

This is an empirical task fMRI study of social perception (perception of emotional crowds and interactions) in healthy adults (N=16; ages 19–27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects ANOVAs) with cluster-corrected maps and tables/figures of activations for main effects and interactions. Full article text including methods, results, and discussion is provided. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objectives and all inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a social interactive sender–receiver game probing deception and theory-of-mind processes (social communication/perception of others), satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=34, ages 21–32), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with Bayesian second-level posterior probability maps and tables of coordinates/figures (e.g., simple deception vs truth, sophisticated deception vs truth), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not a between-group-only contrast, participants are within age range, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study using dyadic (dfMRI) scanning during a social task (face-to-face eye contact), meeting the review’s social-processing requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (group GLM for tasks A and B; paired t-tests for exogenous/endogenous systems), with cluster results, MNI coordinates, atlas labels, and thresholding described (Table 3, Figs 3–5). Thus whole-brain healthy-group results are available. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without task maps, between-group-only contrasts, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly examines social reward processing (social incentive delay task) in healthy adult participants (N=63; ages 20.4–36.6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines social working memory (trait-based ranking) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=25, mean age 21.6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria.

Although this is an empirical fMRI study of social-related tasks in healthy adults and reports voxelwise activation and peak coordinates, the group-level statistical analyses reported in the paper were restricted to a bilateral STS mask rather than presented as unmasked whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample), I6 (coordinates/tables/figures reporting results). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines neural responses during a social-cognitive task (conceptualizing actions at different levels of abstraction, engaging theory-of-mind/mentalizing processes). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI to investigate an imitation/urge-to-imitate paradigm (a social-cognitive process related to perception/understanding of others and social interaction), includes a healthy adult sample aged 18–25 with results reported for that group, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric modulation, SPM8) with cluster-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures. This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (N=33, ages 18–21) that used a social-related task (viewing social vs non-social scenes) and reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (social > non-social contrast; whole-brain random-effects analysis, FDR corrected, with tables and coordinates). This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=15, mean age 23.6) that used a social-related task (viewing two-person violent interactions with attention manipulated to aggressor vs. victim), satisfying I3 and I4. This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=26, ages 19–26) that used a task contrasting social vs non-social reading passages and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (Social>Non-social; Vivid>Abstract) with cluster-corrected thresholds and coordinates (Table 1, figures). This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (passive viewing of in-group/out-group facial expressions; disgust perception), with healthy adult participants (mean age ~21). This fMRI study investigates social communication (speech act comprehension: Naming vs. Requesting) in healthy adult participants (N=18, ages 18–41). This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (dynamic social gestures) in a sample of healthy participants, reporting group-level whole-brain task activation results (cluster-corrected maps and coordinates). This is an fMRI study of social cognition: participants (N=20, healthy adults aged 18–27) performed a task eliciting thoughts about others’ mental states (mentalizing), satisfying I3. This paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review. This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly investigates social processing (linking person perception and person knowledge). This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=24, mean age 25.7) using a social-related task (theory-of-mind/story paradigms contrasting social vs non-social conditions), meeting I3 and I4. This is an empirical fMRI study using the Cyberball (virtual ball-toss) social interaction task (social reward/affiliation), with healthy adult participants (final N=31; ages ~21) and explicit reporting of group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (cluster-level FWE-corrected maps and peak coordinates in text/tables/figures). This is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study using a social interaction task (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) that probes retaliation/provocation—clearly a social-related process. This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (charitable giving, empathy, perspective taking, attentional reorienting) in healthy adult participants (n=33, ages 20–34), meeting the sample criterion.
