Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using the EmpaToM task that probes social cognition (empathy and Theory of Mind) during task performance. The sample includes 178 healthy adult participants (mean age 40.9, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (emotional vs neutral videos for empathy; ToM vs non-ToM questions/videos for mentalizing) entered into random-effects one-sample t-tests and presents activation results in figures/tables. Resting-state and DCM analyses are supplemental but do not replace the reported task-evoked whole-brain maps. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This article reports an fMRI study of social impression updating (social cognition/perception of others), with healthy adult participants (N=21, ages 18–31). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (e.g., L2>F3 whole-brain contrasts, 2×4 ANOVA), reports corrected clusters and peak coordinates in tables and figures, and describes results for the healthy/control group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, imaging acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (whole-brain contrasts, interaction, targeted contrasts), and Discussion, so core content is present and sufficient. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) are met.

This study uses task-based fMRI during a social-related paradigm (naturalistic movie viewing that elicits social cognition and social interaction processing), includes a healthy adult sample (n=34, mean age 22.2), and reports whole-brain voxelwise reverse-correlation results with corrected statistics and visualization (whole-brain χ2 tests, Bonferroni correction; Figure 3). Group-level healthy-participant effects are clearly described. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group only, ages within 18–65, empirical data present). Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, ages 23–33) that uses a social-related task (observing actors grasping objects in angry vs. joyful contexts) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps and contrasts (ANOVA, AG > joyful, angry session > joyful session) with FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This paper reports original fMRI experiments that directly probe social-related processing (sociality manipulations during Prisoner’s Dilemma and Ultimatum/Welfare Games), using healthy adult participants (college-aged, 18+). The manuscript reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (FSL FLAME and SPM12 random-effects; thresholded maps reported at P<0.05 FWE and coordinate tables), and presents activation coordinates and contrasts clearly described for the healthy sample. The full text includes complete methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses attachment-related social stimuli (Adult Attachment Projective Picture System) during task-based fMRI, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (attachment vs. neutral) with cluster-corrected results and MNI coordinates from a healthy adult sample (N=25, ages 19–26). Full methods, results, and discussion are present. No exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports an fMRI experiment probing social cognition (self/other processing, cooperation/competition), fulfilling the social task requirement. Sample: healthy adult participants (final N=24, ages 19–31) meeting the age/sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results (family-wise error cluster-corrected whole-brain contrasts, Table 1 and associated figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements; whole-brain results are described in text and figures (acceptable reporting format). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy or out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of social cooperation using a one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma (social task) with whole-brain task-based analyses reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: PD game/cooperation), I4 (healthy adult sample; final analyzed N=18, mean age 21.04, within 18–65), I5 (group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses reported with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and tables of coordinates), I6 (whole-brain results reported as coordinate tables/contrast descriptions). No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not an only between-group contrast, participants within age range, and this is empirical data. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplemental XLSX references do not prevent treating the core article as complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study using a social-related task (valence judgments of naturalistic social interactions) in a healthy adult sample (N=38, ages 18–30). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., Social > Non-social contrasts; full-factorial ANOVA) with FWE correction and provides activation tables/figures and coordinates. Results are for the healthy/control group (no clinical subgroup only reporting). The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or out-of-range ages) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of emotion regulation using angry faces (a social stimulus) with healthy adult participants (N=60, age range 18–57). The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., Observe-angry > Observe-neutral; Decrease vs Observe-angry) with coordinates, tables, and figures describing healthy-group effects. Resting-state analyses are additional but the study includes task-evoked whole-brain results for the healthy sample. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not between-group-only, sample within 18–65, and empirical). Hence it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study of prosocial (social) learning in healthy adults. It meets I3: uses task-based fMRI targeting social/prosocial processing; I4: sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=31, ages 19–32) with results reported for the healthy group; I5: reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and peak coordinates (with voxelwise/FWE/SVC results and tables/figures); I6: whole-brain results are clearly described in the text, tables, and figures (including supplemental tables). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=25 females, mean age 23.2). Participants performed a social (mentalizing) task about friends and kin during task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (friend > kin contrast and parametric linear analyses across network layers) with cluster-thresholding, tables of clusters/coordinates, and figures. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears to be a complete full text. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (task fMRI of social processing), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from healthy group), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply.

Study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=10, mean age 25) using a Face Matching Task assessing perception of others’ emotions (social-related processing). The paper includes group-level, whole-brain GLM analyses (one-sample t-tests for contrasts: neutral+fear > control; fear > neutral; fear > neutral+control) reported at second level (results referenced in main text and Supplementary Material), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. The study therefore satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps for healthy group), and I6 (maps/results described and available in supplement). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions).

This paper reports an fMRI experiment manipulating social competition (a social-related task involving social comparison/mentalizing). Sample: healthy adult participants (female, ages 18–35; N=20 after exclusion), satisfying the adult healthy-sample criterion. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses and contrasts (e.g., competition > no-competition; working-memory parametric modulators), including cluster thresholds, Monte Carlo correction, peak coordinates, and figures/tables describing whole-brain results. Whole-brain results are explicitly described for the healthy/control group (not limited to a narrow subgroup). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, age outside range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It uses task-based fMRI to probe a social cognition construct (empathy for pain) (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants aged 18–40 with group-level results reported separately (stress and control healthy groups) (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical analyses with family-wise error correction and presents whole-brain results (figures and coordinate tables) for contrasts (e.g., INJECTION>QTIP and BIOPSY>QTIP) and group comparisons (I5, I6). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16–17 analyzed per task; age range 21–46) that directly probes social-related processing (attribution/understanding of emotions in humans and non-human animals). The paper reports whole-brain group-level analyses (conjunctions, cluster-level FWE correction) and ROI and whole-brain results, with statistical maps and tabulated results described (meeting acceptable reporting formats). All required content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (reports whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in acceptable formats). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group task effects, empirical data in healthy adults).

This is a task-based fMRI study of social perception (decoding emotion/age from faces) in healthy adults (final N=25, ages 21–33), and reports group-level whole-brain analyses (random-effects faces > objects contrast and whole-brain searchlight results, with tables/figures). The healthy/control group results are reported clearly for the within-group effects. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This article reports an event-related fMRI study of social interaction (SI) recognition (a social-related task) using point-light displays (meets I3). It includes a healthy adult group (N=16, ages 20–41) with results reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (SI > NM) for the adult group using SPM8 with peak- and cluster-level thresholding and FWE corrections; activations for adults (e.g., bilateral pMTG/pSTS, IFG, dmPFC, caudate) are explicitly described (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, adult group within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that probes social-related processing (self-related and mentalizing/social cognition) during an article-reading/sharing task and links neural activity to behavior. Participants were healthy adults aged 18–24 in two samples (n=41 and n=39), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses and exploratory whole-brain maps and cluster tables (SI Fig. S3 and Table S5) with multiple-comparison corrections and permutation testing, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. The manuscript contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and whole-brain results are described in the text and supplements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and this is empirical work).

This is an fMRI study of person-related (social) memory and knowledge retrieval (status, personality traits, identity), using task fMRI in healthy adult participants (Study 1: n=24, Mage≈23; Study 2: n=26, Mage≈20). The paper reports group-level whole-brain univariate GLM contrasts (e.g., all memory > baseline; status > baseline; trait > baseline; face > name; name > face) thresholded at voxel-level FWE P<0.05 and provides coordinates/tables and figures for these maps. Thus it satisfies social task fMRI (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and reports whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps (I5), with acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state/only connectivity, no between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalising/theory of mind) in healthy adults. It reports task-based fMRI with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level random-effects ANOVAs), thresholded to whole-brain-corrected significance and summarized in Table 1 and figures (contrasts such as mentalising>factual and parametric modulation). Participants are healthy adults within 18–65 (Experiment 2 mean age 22; Experiment 1 range 18–60). Whole-brain results are clearly reported in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=41 analyzed; ages 18–24) that directly probes social-related processing (decisions to share with others, perspective-taking, social-cognition ROIs). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task activation analyses (select > content, share > content, share > select) with family-wise error correction and tables/figures of activations, clearly from the healthy sample. Thus it satisfies I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (implicit and explicit theory-of-mind) in healthy adults using a Sally–Anne type paradigm, meeting the review objective. Sample: 33 recruited, N=22 analyzed, mean age 24.4 (within 18–65), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports a group-level whole-brain random-effects GLM for the explicit general-belief localizer (contrasting false-belief vs false-photograph) and provides voxelwise results/coordinates (q(FDR)<0.05; Fig.2A and peak Talairach coordinates), which are clearly identified as coming from the healthy group. Although the primary implicit ToM contrast was analyzed with an ROI approach, the presence of the whole-brain localizer map satisfies the whole-brain results inclusion (acceptable per I6). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind) in healthy adult participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the analyses are ROI-based MVPA and regionwise tests; the full text does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group (no whole-brain activation map, coordinates table, or clearly described group-level voxelwise contrast is reported in the provided content). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence). It is excluded under E2 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results).

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of social perception in healthy adults (N=14, ages 20–32) using tasks that explicitly probe perception/understanding of others (point-light and shape-animation social interaction stimuli). It includes group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported peaks/figures (interaction > independent; animate > physical) and reports coordinates and maps, satisfying whole-brain evidence. The healthy adult sample is within 18–65 and results are reported for that group. The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, figures, supplemental movies referenced) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception (impression formation of others varying in race and socioeconomic status), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=60, mean age 23.8), satisfying the age and healthy-sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain second-level GLMs (exploratory whole-brain regressions with voxel-wise thresholds and reported clusters/figures; full results referenced in Supplementary Material S4), providing voxelwise task-evoked maps for the healthy group. Whole-brain results are reported in text/figures and coordinate/cluster information is available, meeting the reporting criterion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an fMRI experiment explicitly probing social perception (judging facing-toward vs away of point-light and human-like walkers), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (N=16, mean age 22.75) within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (ANOVAs, contrasts) with stereotaxic coordinates and thresholding (p<0.05 FWE) and tables/figures of activation; thus whole-brain evidence is available and reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Accordingly inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study used fMRI with social/attachment narratives and enrolled healthy adult participants (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the paper reports only resting-state, seed-based functional connectivity analyses (post-narrative FC) and does not present any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for the healthy/control group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only seed-based/resting-state connectivity reported without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI task examining social interaction processing (affective and cooperative interactions), satisfying the review’s social-related construct (I3). Sample consists of 36 healthy adult participants (ages ~24–25), meeting the sample criterion (I4). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects group analysis; results thresholded and reported with cluster FDR p<.05; tables and figures of activations), fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). The supplied full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of joint social interaction (leading/following/mutual) with haptic contact, directly addressing social-processing constructs (social communication, perception of others, mentalizing, social reward). Sample comprises healthy adult dancers (mean age 40.4, within 18–65) with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (contrasts, FDR-corrected maps, and tables of Talairach coordinates), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting (figures/tables and text). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study includes a task-based fMRI social cognition contrast (TOM vs Random) performed in a large sample of healthy adult participants from the Human Connectome Project (ages 22–>35), and provides group-level whole-brain task activation maps (reported and thresholded; Cohen's d and level-3 z maps are described). Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly reported and visualized, satisfying reporting via figures/tables and supplementary materials. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (acceptable forms of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The paper reports an fMRI study of social decision-making (modified iterated prisoner's dilemma) in healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 23–38). It includes whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (conjunction and task contrasts such as COMP>COOP), cluster-level multiple-comparison correction, and reports results in figures/tables (coordinates and SPMs). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, limitations) is present. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

All inclusion criteria are met. I3: The study used task-based fMRI contrasting social vs. non-social images (valence appraisal task), isolating social-related processing. I4: The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=14 analyzed; ages 23–50), with psychiatric screening and separate reporting of healthy-group results. I5: The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (social–nonsocial contrast, voxel thresholding, FDR-corrected cluster results, conjunction maps). I6: Whole-brain results are presented in figures and cluster tables and clearly described in the text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review objective of identifying fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This study reports an fMRI task probing emotion perception (perception/understanding of others; social communication) using dynamic facial and vocal stimuli — clearly a social-related task. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (ages 19–24 and mean 19.67), reported separately. The paper presents voxelwise, whole-brain task-evoked group analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA, whole-brain contrasts, PFWE<0.05) with tables/figures of activations rather than ROI-only results. Whole-brain results for the healthy/control group are clearly described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical restrictions).

Only abstract and metadata provided (full text incomplete). From the abstract, the study uses task fMRI in a social decision context, so I3 (functional MRI during a social-related task) appears satisfied. However, the provided content does not report participant ages (cannot confirm 18–65), nor does it provide methods/results to verify a group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (I5) or that whole-brain results are reported in acceptable formats (I6). Therefore I4, I5, and I6 cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be reliably applied based on the incomplete text. Recommend obtaining the full text to verify age range and whether whole-brain task activation maps are reported before inclusion.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract provided). The abstract indicates this is an fMRI study of prosodic categorisation relevant to social communication (meets I3). However, the available text does not confirm key required details: participant sample characteristics and age range (I4) are not reported in the abstract, and it is not possible to verify that the paper reports at least one group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map for the healthy/control group (I5/I6). Because these inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the provided content, the study cannot be included based on the available information. No exclusion criteria E2–E6 are explicitly met from the abstract alone.

This paper meets all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis objective. It uses task-based fMRI during social-related processing (self-evaluation and endorsement of others’ evaluation of the self), satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults (final N=31, ages 19–24), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (contrasts and a whole-brain multiple regression with cluster-level FWE correction), with coordinates/tables/figures, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Tables/Figures, and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65).

This study includes an fMRI social-cognition task (social interaction vs. random movement) and reports group-level task activation analyses. Participants are healthy adults from HCP (ages 22–36+; n≈100) and UCLA (ages 21–50; n=114), satisfying the age and sample requirements. The paper describes voxel-wise GLM activation analyses and presents group-level activation results (e.g., Figure 1 and accompanying text), fulfilling the whole-brain task-evoked map requirement. Reporting formats include figures and supplementary material; these are clearly identified as healthy/control group results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without activation maps, not between-group-only, ages within range, and empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review.

Full text is unavailable (404 Not Found on publisher site), so core article content (methods, results) cannot be reviewed. Therefore I cannot verify inclusion criteria: I3 (use of fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), or I5/I6 (reporting of group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps). No exclusion criteria can be confirmed from the available metadata. Because essential information is missing, the study is excluded pending retrieval of the full text.

This full text meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI during social cognition (mental-state/judgment task), (I4) reports a healthy adult sample (N=28 after exclusion; ages 18–22), (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (searchlight RSA and repetition-suppression voxelwise maps with permutation TFCE correction), and (I6) whole-brain results are clearly described and reported in figures and text. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion requirements for the review: (1) It uses task-based fMRI during an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma, a social decision-making task (I3). (2) The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=20 males, ages 21–37) with results reported for the healthy group (I4). (3) The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (one-sample t tests, flexible factorial analyses, MDMA vs placebo contrasts) with cluster-level FWE correction and tabulated activations (I5). (4) Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures and described in the text (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROIs only, are not solely connectivity/resting-state, and are not only between-group or non-healthy samples. The supplied full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical dual-fMRI hyperscanning study in healthy adults (N=44, mean age 22.37) using a social interaction task (pattern game) that manipulates cooperation/competition and concurrent/turn-based interaction—clearly a social-related task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results with non-parametric permutation correction and presents cluster coordinates and figures (Tables 1–3, Fig. 4), satisfying whole-brain reporting (coordinates/figures). All inclusion criteria are met (I3: fMRI social task; I4: healthy adult sample reported; I5: group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported; I6: whole-brain results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text content provided appears incomplete (only title, authors, journal metadata; no Introduction/Methods/Results/Discussion). Unable to verify key inclusion criteria: I3 (use of fMRI during a social-related task) cannot be confirmed from provided text; I4 (healthy adult group 18–65 reported separately) cannot be confirmed; I5 (reports at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked map for healthy/control group) cannot be confirmed; I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/supplement) cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria can be confidently identified from the incomplete content. Because the full text is incomplete and essential methodological/results information are missing, the study cannot be judged eligible for inclusion at this stage.

Full text content provided is limited to abstract/highlights/metadata; core article (methods, full results, figures/tables) not available to verify required whole-brain task activation reporting. From abstract: I3 (task-based fMRI of social processing – theory of mind) and I4 (includes healthy younger adult group) appear satisfied. However I5 (reports at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group) cannot be confirmed from the available content, and I6 (acceptable reporting forms) also cannot be verified. No explicit exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are demonstrably met from the abstract alone. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm necessary whole-brain task activation results and must exclude pending full-text review.

This is an fMRI study of face perception/recognition (social perception of others), using functional MRI during task-based viewing of faces (Experiment 1) and behavioral tasks linked to fMRI data (Experiments 2–3), meeting the social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (ages reported, mean ages in 20s; n=20 in main fMRI experiment), satisfying the sample criterion. The methods describe group-level, whole-brain mixed-effects (FLAME) analyses and an independent localizer contrast (faces vs scrambled) used to define ROIs from group data, indicating group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps are reported/used. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (only ROI analyses, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This is an fMRI study of social processing using live bidirectional conversation (human–human vs human–robot) — a clearly social-related task probing mentalizing and social motivation. Sample: 21 healthy adult participants (mean age 25.8, no psychiatric/neurological history), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (HHI vs HRI and reverse), with statistical inference (p<0.05 FDR-corrected cluster-level) and whole-brain maps/figures; group data are available on NeuroVault/OpenNeuro. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI study that directly probes social-related processing (empathy for pain/pleasure when observing human and robot agents) using task-based functional MRI (meets I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants aged 18–27 with results reported for the healthy group (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects task activation analyses (repetition suppression and discrete event-related contrasts), with cluster-corrected results and whole-brain maps referenced and deposited on NeuroVault (meets I5 and I6). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; core content is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This empirical fMRI study (n=51 healthy adults, mean age 22.5) directly investigates social processing (perception of others’ dynamic facial expressions). It reports group-level, whole-brain, voxel-wise task activation contrasts (dynamic facial expressions vs. dynamic mosaics) with appropriate random-effects analyses and FWE-corrected thresholds, with results shown in tables and figures. All inclusion criteria (I3: fMRI social-related task; I4: healthy adult sample 18–65; I5: whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps; I6: results clearly reported in text/figures/tables) are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study examines vocal emotional processing in healthy adults (I3 and I4 satisfied) but does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps from the healthy group. Instead, results are reported as ROI-based functional connectivity and graph-theoretical network metrics. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E3 (connectivity/graph analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E2 (only ROI/parcellation-based analyses with no voxelwise whole-brain task results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related task: vocal emotion/social communication) and I4 (healthy adult sample 20–35). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that uses task-based paradigms probing social processing (take advice game and trust game) with fMRI acquisition and analyses. The sample consists of 31 healthy adult participants (age 24.3±3.8), satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain task-evoked results (searchlight MVPA and whole-brain univariate contrasts) clearly identified as group-level effects for the healthy participant group, with cluster- and voxel-level corrected maps and tables described in the text and supplementary materials. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, neuroimaging acquisition and preprocessing, and statistical analyses, so the full text is complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports task-based fMRI during observation of socio-affective touch (a clearly social-related task) and includes a healthy adult control group (21 neurotypical adults, age-matched). The manuscript provides group-level whole-brain task results for the healthy/control group (mean group effects and brain areas activated for social vs. non-social touch), with MNI coordinates and figures reported in the main text and Additional file 1 (Figure S2 and Table S2), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked maps. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and participants are within 18–65).
